claims.claim: MongoDB links developer data models and operational databases to cloud/application infrastructure; the human-need bridge is faster construction and operation of data-rich software, while the structural bottleneck is developer adoption plus reliable scalable data operations rather than raw compute ownership.

Atlas improves deployment portability across cloud environments, but successor bottlenecks include cloud consumption economics, workload portability, hyperscaler-native substitutes and the ability to convert AI application growth into durable database consumption.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Developer mindshare and a managed data platform can control an application-layer bottleneck, but underlying cloud infrastructure remains outside MongoDB's control.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Document-model/developer fit supports persistence, while hyperscaler databases, relational/open-source alternatives and new AI-oriented data architectures remain substitutes.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Database demand spans conventional and AI applications, although consumption growth varies with customer workloads.

causalEdges.mechanism: document database and managed services reduce application data-model and operations friction
Atlas depends on cloud infrastructure to run managed database workloads
operational data services support application state and retrieval

risks.risk: Cloud dependence and substitute databases can shift bargaining power or reduce workload capture even if application data volumes grow.

unknowns.unknown: Measurable AI-driven Atlas consumption contribution remains unproven ahead of future disclosures.

claims.claim: Strong 30% revenue and ~29% Atlas growth do not by themselves establish AI monetization or future acceleration; those remain separate claims requiring workload-level evidence.

Stock-based compensation remains economically material: MongoDB reported $148.9M of SBC in Q2 FY2027 and $286.8M for the first six months, creating dilution/owner-economics pressure even when non-GAAP operating measures improve.

factors.name: dilutionRisk
factors.basis: Q2 FY2027 stock-based compensation was about $148.9M and six-month SBC about $286.8M.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: AI optionality should not be counted as realized monetization without measured incremental Atlas consumption.

risks.risk: SBC dilution, hyperscaler/native database competition, cloud consumption variability and narrative expectations can weaken per-share conversion of operating growth.

contradictions.claim: Strong total growth versus uncertain Atlas acceleration
contradictions.resolution: Current growth is observed; future acceleration and AI contribution remain unproven rather than assumed.

unknowns.unknown: Future SBC trajectory, net-new versus expansion contribution and measurable AI workload contribution remain uncertain.
